rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is voiced on the Day of Resurrection from the sacred presence, either by God or by the angels.
rows.anchor: فهذا قول يصدر يوم القيامة من جانب القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God speaks, naming the Lord instead of using a pronoun underscores intimate care and honors the addressed soul through the possessive relation.
rows.anchor: إظهاراً في مقام الإِضمار بقرينة تفريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels speak, ‘your Lord’ is the expected wording; the following ‘enter among My servants’ is God's prompting that confirms their words.
rows.anchor: جرى على مقتضى الظاهر وعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God figuratively means dwelling in honored Paradise, like a host's home; the soul earned it through promised good deeds and had been away in worldly life, so this is a special return rather than mere afterlife arrival.
rows.anchor: والرجوع إلى الله مستعار للكون في نعيم الجنة التي هي دار الكرامة عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of an honored dwelling is illustrated by the seat of truth with the Mighty King.
rows.anchor: دار الكرامة عند الله بمنزلة دار المضيف قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this may begin a new address to the tranquil souls of believers, prompted by the preceding mention of punishment for the disbelieving human.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الآية استئنافاً ابتدائياً جرى على مناسبة ذكر عذاب الإنسان المشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to return is meant as a promise qualified by the following states, ‘pleased’ and ‘approved’; return is figurative on this reading.
rows.anchor: مراد منه تقييده بالحالين بعده وهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive forms ‘My servants’ and ‘My Garden’ shift from third-person reference to first-person speech.
rows.anchor: التفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan when he donated the well of Rumah.
rows.anchor: أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان لما تصدق ببئرِ رومة

rows.speaker: بريدة
rows.claim: Buraydah says the verse was revealed about Hamza when he was killed.
rows.anchor: أنها نزلت في حمزة حين قُتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report identifies Khubayb ibn Adi when the people of Mecca crucified him.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خُبَيب بن عدي لما صلبه أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is agreed to be Meccan, though al-Dani transmits from some scholars that it is Medinan.
rows.anchor: والاتفاق على أن السورة مكية إلا ما رواه الداني عن بعض العلماء أنها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse is Medinan, it is either detached from what precedes by a specific divine arrangement or revealed later because of thematic fit.
rows.anchor: وهي على هذا منفصلة عما قبلها كتبت هنا بتوقيف خاص أو نزلت عقب ما قبلها للمناسبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Harithah, Ubayy ibn Kab, and Ibn Masud say this is said at resurrection as spirits return to bodies.
rows.anchor: أن هذا يقال عند البعث لترجع الأرواح في الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the resurrection reading, the passage continues the account of the earth being crushed; return is literal and ‘Lord’ means the soul's possessor, its body.
rows.anchor: والرجوع على هذا حقيقة والرب مراد به صاحب النفس وهو الجسد

rows.speaker: زيد بن حارثة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Salih say the address is spoken to the soul at death.
rows.anchor: يقال هذا للنفس عند الموت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr relates that a man recited the verse, Abu Bakr praised it, and the Prophet said an angel would say it to Abu Bakr at death.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم « أمَا إنَّ الملَك سيقولها لك عند الموت

rows.speaker: زيد بن حارثة
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Harithah says the words greet a believer's soul at death with glad tidings of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن زيد بن حارثة أن هذا يقال لنفس المؤمن عند الموت تبشر بالجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean the whole person, as in verses about regret over neglect and the prohibition on unlawful killing.
rows.anchor: تطلق على الذات كلها كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can also mean the spirit that gives the body life, as in the verse describing the soul that urges evil.
rows.anchor: وتطلق على الروح التي بها حياة الجسد كما في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutmaʾinna is an active participle of itmaʾanna, meaning calm, untroubled, and undisturbed.
rows.anchor: اسم فاعل من اطمأن إذا كان هادئاً غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is a soul settled by belief in the Quran without doubt or hesitation; this praises its faith.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون من سكون النفس بالتصديق لما جاء به القرآن دون تردد ولا اضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may describe the soul's quiet security in the afterlife, without fear or trial.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من هدوء النفس بدون خوف ولا فتنة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: The author regards Abu Amr's analysis as more correct: the first radical is hamzated and mīm is the root's second radical.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh derives the verb from ṭaʾmana, with metathesis placing mīm before hamza; this gives muṭaʾminna and verbal noun iṭmiʾnān.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه : أصل الفعل : طَأْمَنَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective need not identify or restrict the addressees, who would not know they were tranquil until admitted; it instead praises them, explains the good news, and assures them of safety.
rows.anchor: فالوصف مراد به الثناء والإيماء إلى وجه بناء الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God may inspire the souls to recognize their tranquility, making the adjective identifying or restrictive.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون للتعريف أو التخصيص بأن يجعل الله إلهاماً في قلوبهم يعرفون به أنهم مطمئنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tranquility is figurative for contentment and certainty about one's fate: believers trusted the messengers in life and see signs of favor at resurrection, unlike the doomed.
rows.anchor: والاطمئنان : مجاز في طيب النفس وعدم ترددها في مصيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certainty in God's existence and oneness, trust in His promise, and sincerity in deeds are intended constituents of tranquility, individually and together.
rows.anchor: ولا جرم أن ذلك كله من مقومات الاطمئنان المقصود فمجموعه مراد وأجزاؤه مقصودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the souls received glad tidings of Paradise before being called to enter it.
rows.anchor: قبل ندائهم ثم نودوا بأن يدخلوا الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is pleased with the honor it receives, implying that it is given everything it desires.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية عن إعطائها كل ما تطمح إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mardiyya is a passive participle originally meaning ‘one approved of’; deletion and verbal connection remove the preposition and make it the grammatical subject.
rows.anchor: والمرضية : اسم مفعول وأصله : مَرضياً عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being approved adds praise and implies that the one pleased with her increases His gifts beyond what she already finds satisfactory.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا الوصف زيادة الثناء مع الكناية عن الزيادة في إفاضة الإنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two commands spell out the preceding general good news; this detail after summary renews the recipients' joy.
rows.anchor: فهو تفصيل بعد الإجمال لتكرير إدخال السرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Among My servants’ means joining the company of the righteous, indicated by the possessive context and pairing with ‘My Garden’.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : ادخلي في زمرة عبادي . والمراد العباد الصالحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parallels the promise to admit believers among the righteous.
rows.anchor: ومعنى هذا كقوله تعالى : { لندخلنهم في الصالحين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition expresses real inclusion, which amounts to companionship with those blessed by God.
rows.anchor: فالظرفية حقيقية وتؤول إلى معنى المعية كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive ‘My Garden’ honors Paradise, as does the description of a seat of truth with the Mighty King.
rows.anchor: وإضافة ( جنة ) إلى ضمير الجلالة إضافة تشريف كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This possessive makes the shift to first-person speech especially fitting after ‘your Lord’ was spoken in third person.
rows.anchor: وهذه الإضافة هي مما يزيد الالتفات إلى ضمير التكلُّم حسناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating ‘enter’ rather than combining the phrases emphasizes entry into the Garden and intensifies the recipients' joy.
rows.anchor: وتكرير فعل { وادخلي } فلم يقل : فادخلي جنتي في عبادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse adds blameworthy speech to the human's inner faults: false boasting and self-praise for spending wealth wastefully rather than wisely.
rows.anchor: أعقبت مساوي نفسه بمذام أقواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs bragged about dissipating wealth and treated it as virtue because it suggested they did not care about their money.
rows.anchor: وقد كان أهل الجاهلية يتبجحون بإتلاف المال ويعدونه منقبة لإيذانه بقلة اكتراث صاحبه به

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antarah boasts of spending his wealth while keeping his honor intact, illustrating the pre-Islamic pride in lavish expenditure.
rows.anchor: قال عنترة : وإذا سَكِرْتُ فإنَّنِي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He says’ is circumstantial with ‘the human’ in the preceding verse; this boasting is part of the hardship described there.
rows.anchor: { يقول أهلكت مالاً } في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question clause is an explicative supplement to ‘I spent much wealth’: the boaster supposes everyone believes him, though some know he lies.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { يقول أهلكت مالاً }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse supports the point that a person's character becomes known even when he thinks it is hidden.
rows.anchor: قال زهير : ومهما تكن عند امرىء من خليقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative rebukes the boaster and implies that God knows his inner state and that his generosity claim is false.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إنكار وتوبيخ وهو كناية عن علم الله تعالى بدخيلته وأن افتخاره بالكرم باطل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read lubadan with an ungeminated bāʾ, a plural of lubda for wool or hair matted and stuck together.
rows.anchor: بضم اللام وفتح الموحدة في قراءة الجمهور

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jafar reads lubbadan with a doubled bāʾ, either as a plural of lābid (‘gathered’) or a fuʿʿal noun like zummal and jubbaʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر { لبَّداً } بضم اللام وتشديد الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the statement that the soul prospers is parenthetical, this verse answers the oath together with verse 14; the oath-response lām is omitted to shorten the long oath.
rows.anchor: لام الجواب محذوف تخفيفاً لاستطالة القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted oath lām is comparable to the oath in al-Buruj, where the response follows a long series of oaths.
rows.anchor: وقد مثلوا لحذف اللام بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage threatens Quraysh, who knowingly defied the Messenger like Thamud; their destruction came through the swords of those they opposed, abused, and expelled.
rows.anchor: التعريض بتهديد المشركين الذين كذبوا الرسول طغياناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath warns that Quraysh may be punished as Thamud were, because they failed to understand that Thamud's annihilation followed rejection of their messenger.
rows.anchor: ليصيبكم عذابٌ كما أصاب ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘denied’ is omitted but supplied by the next verse: they denied their Messenger.
rows.anchor: محذوف لدلالة قوله بعده : { فقال لهم رسول الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks cause; ṭaghwā is a verbal noun of ṭaghā, meaning excessive arrogance.
rows.anchor: وباء { بطغواها } للسببية ، أي كانت طغواها سبب تكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's rejection arose from pride that kept them from following someone they considered inferior, as their demand for a notable recipient of revelation shows.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعريض بتنظير مشركي قريش في تكذيبهم بثمود في أن سبب تكذيبهم هو الطغيان والتكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of the most wretched man's rising is brought forward because his act is part of their transgression and tied to denial; its placement shows their incitement, while hamstringing still followed the Messenger's warning.
rows.anchor: لأن انبعاث أشقاها لعقر الناقة جزئي من جزئيات طغواهم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes identify the most wretched man as Qudar ibn Salif; he surpassed the others by personally committing the crime despite their collective incitement.
rows.anchor: وعني به رجل منهم سماه المفسرون قُدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ can coordinate with ‘Thamud denied,’ giving normal sequence: after denying Salih, they received the she-camel sign and warning not to harm it or deny its watering turn.
rows.anchor: عاطفة على { كذبت } فتفيد الترتيب والتعقيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this sequence, the later denial rejects the threat implicit in the warning; the she-camel sign came after their first rejection, as is usual for prophetic signs and apparent in Hud.
rows.anchor: أي فيما أنذرهم به فعقروها بالتكذيب المذكور أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fāʾ gives only textual sequence, moving from a summary of Thamud's denial to its details; then ‘when their most wretched arose’ need not be treated as fronted from later.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للترتيب الذكري المجرد وهي تفيد عطف مفصل على مجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural pronouns return because Thamud is now treated as a people, whereas earlier pronouns followed the tribe's collective name.
rows.anchor: وأعيدت عليهم ضمائر الجمع باعتبار أنهم جمع وإن كانت الضمائر قبله مراعىً فيها أن ثمود اسم قبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāqata Allāh is accusative as a warning, with an implied ‘beware’; the warning is really against harming the she-camel, expressed by attaching the command to the entity.
rows.anchor: على التحذير ، والتقدير : احذروا ناقة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel is attributed to God because He made it a sign of Salih's truth and its emergence was beyond customary causes.
rows.anchor: وإضافة { ناقة } إلى اسم الجلالة لأنها آية جعلها الله على صدق رسالة صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suqyā is a verbal noun of saqā, coordinated with the warning: beware her watering, meaning do not usurp her allotted drink.
rows.anchor: والسقيا : اسم مصدر سَقى ، وهو معطوف على التحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construction supplies an omitted noun: ‘beware her watering’ means do not seize her allotted share.
rows.anchor: أي احذروا غصب سقيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verbal noun names the water itself by using the source for its object; context warns against watering their camels on her allotted day.
rows.anchor: أو أطلق السقيا على الماء الذي تسقى منه إطلاقاً للمصدر على المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context and word suqyā indicate a warning against letting their camels drink from the water on the she-camel's day.
rows.anchor: فإن مادة سقيا تؤذن بأن المراد التحذير من أن يسقوا إبلهم من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied threat was explicit in the command not to touch the camel with harm, lest painful punishment seize them.
rows.anchor: وهو المصرح به في آية سورة الأعراف ( 73 ) في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their response denial is apt because they rejected the threat of punishment contained in the Messenger's warning, even though the warning itself was an imperative.
rows.anchor: وبهذا الاعتبار استقام التعبير عن مقابلة التحذير بالتكذيب مع أن التحذير إنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAqr wounds a camel's forelegs so pain makes it kneel for slaughter at the breast; by close association, it conventionally means slaughtering it.
rows.anchor: والعَقْر : جرح البعير في يديه ليبرك على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama means God cried out against them in anger: the sound of the thunderclap and earthquake by which they were destroyed.
rows.anchor: أي صاح عليهم ربهم صيحة غضب . والمراد بهذه الدمدمة صوت الصاعقة والرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction by a cry is compared with the account that the people were seized by the cry.
rows.anchor: التي أهلكوا بها قال تعالى : { فأخذتهم الصيحة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the cry to God is a figurative attribution of its cause, since God creates the cry and its qualities.
rows.anchor: وإسناد ذلك إلى الله مجاز عقلي لأن الله هو خالق الصيحة وكيفياتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama follows the quadriliteral faʿlala pattern.
rows.anchor: فوزن دمدم فعلل

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take damdama to mean covering them with earth, deriving it from covering a grave; repetition intensifies the sense, like kabkaba.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين : دمدم عليهم أطبق عليهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the ‘covered with earth’ interpretation, damdama repeats dammama for emphasis, like kabkaba.
rows.anchor: ودمدم مكرر دمم للمبالغة مثل كبكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads ‘then He leveled it’ as their all being alike in destruction; the feminine pronoun refers to the damdama inferred from the verb.
rows.anchor: فضمير النصب عائد إلى الدمدمة المأخوذة من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who read damdama as covering them with earth take ‘leveled it’ to mean flattening earth over them, hiding bodies and dwellings; the pronoun then means earth.
rows.anchor: جعل الأرض مستوية عليهم لا تظهر فيها أجسادهم ولا بلادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that alternative reading, the wording resembles the image of the earth being leveled over people.
rows.anchor: وجعلوا ضمير المؤنث عائداً إلى الأرض المفهومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is complete paronomasia between ‘fa-sawwāhā’ here and the earlier ‘wa-mā sawwāhā’.
rows.anchor: وبين { فسواها } هنا وقوله : { وما سواها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUqbā is what follows an act as a consequence or reward for its doer.
rows.anchor: والعقبى : ما يحصل عقب فعل من الأفعال من تبعة لفاعله أو مثوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People expect the defeated to seek revenge and the victor to fear retaliation; saying God fears no aftermath implies His power to punish disbelievers and that delayed punishment is respite, not weakness, and closes the passage.
rows.anchor: فكان الذي يغلب غيره يتقي حذراً من أن يتمكن مغلوبه من الثأر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase depicts total annihilation: no survivor remains to avenge the people, as when a whole group is wiped out.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قوله : { فلا يخاف عقباها } تمثيلاً لحالهم في الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ammā elaborates the summary that striving differs; ammā carries both conditional force and the function of dividing the account into cases.
rows.anchor: تفريع وتفصيل للإجمال في قوله : { إن سعيكم لشتى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafṣīl distinguishes members of a previously shared group by a difference important to the discussion.
rows.anchor: والتفصيل : التفكيك بين متعدد اشتركت آحاده في حالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject needing division is striving, but the text divides by describing strivers; because actions accompany agents, this eloquent shift conveys both meanings.
rows.anchor: والمحتاج للتفصيل هنا هو السعي المذكور ، ولكن جعل التفصيل ببيان الساعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from an action to its agent is illustrated by the poet's fear exceeding that of a watchful ibex.
rows.anchor: كقول النابغة : وقد خِفت حتى ما تزيد مخافتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples express a quality through the person who has it, including ‘righteousness is whoever believes’ and comparison with a believer's faith.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two main groups may be those enabled toward ease and those toward hardship, encompassing different deeds and serving exhortation and warning.
rows.anchor: فريق ميسر لليسرى وفريق ميسر للعسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division is also illustrated by the day people emerge separately to see their deeds, including outcomes of even the smallest good or evil.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { يومئذٍ يصدر الناس أشتاتاً ليروا أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the groups are the two sets of three traits stated in verses 5 and 8–9, a valid division of varied striving.
rows.anchor: واتّقى وصدّق بالحسنى ، ومنْ بخل واستغنى وكذب بالحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Whoever’ is general, covering everyone who gives, is mindful of God, and affirms the good promise.
rows.anchor: يعُم كل من يفعل الإعطاء ويتقي ويصدِّق بالحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ungraded occasion report links the verse to Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf and freeing him to save him from torture.
rows.anchor: وروي أن هذا نزل بسبب أن أبا بكر اشترى بلالاً من أمية

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes substitute Abu Sufyan ibn Harb for Umayya ibn Khalaf in the report; the author calls this an error.
rows.anchor: أبا سفيان بن حرب عوضَ أمية بن خلف ، وهم وهَم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported occasion concerns Abu al-Dahdah and a hypocrite; this would imply a Medinan sūra, but an occasion does not restrict the verse's general application.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في قضية أبي الدحداح مع رجل منافق ستأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘gave’ is omitted because giving without return commonly means giving money; the intended giving is alms.
rows.anchor: لأن فعل الإعطاء إذا أريد به إعطاء المال بدون عوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘was mindful’ is omitted because the understood object is God.
rows.anchor: لأنه يعلم أن المقدّر اتّقى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving, God-consciousness, and belief in the good promise are traits of faith, so the description means being among believers.
rows.anchor: وهذه الخلال الثلاث من خلال الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement of Hell's denizens that they did not pray or feed the poor means they were not believers.
rows.anchor: أي لم نك من أهل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘was miserly’ is omitted because the intended miserliness is with wealth.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر متعلقه لأنه أريد به البخل بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istighnā is set against God-consciousness: the persistent unbeliever considers himself independent of obeying God and His call, relying on idols and his people.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به الاستغناء عن امتثال أمر الله ودعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes the augmentative sīn and tāʾ as intensifying the action, as with istajāba (‘answered’).
rows.anchor: فالسين والتاء للمبالغة في الفعل مثل سين استحباب بمعنى أجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the augmentative letters mark seeking: the person seeks greater wealth through miserliness.
rows.anchor: وقد يراد به زيادة طلب الغنى بالبخل بالمال ، فتكون السين والتاء للطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together, the three traits characterize a polytheist.
rows.anchor: وهذه الخلال كناية عن كونه من المشركين
